messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Performing a replicate study using INLA. Are all the results the same ?
parts:
Apart from the slight numerical differences due to parallelisation, inla is a deterministic method for obtaining estimates of Bayesian posterior distributions. MCMC is a stochastic method for obtaining such estimates. You should expect to get different results from each MCMC run due to the inherent randomness (unless you use the same random seed each time), but inla should be expected to give the same answer each time. It’s a classic variance/bias tradeoff: MCMC has large variance but (hopefully) no bias. Inla has no variance but does have a small bias.

You need to ask yourself _why_ you would want different results from inla each time.
The suggestion of using inla.posterior.sample() just turns one step of inla into a Monte Carlo (independent samples, not MCMC) sampler, which is useful in some situations, but it’s not clear from your question what it is you’re actually indenting to achieve.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Performing a replicate study using INLA. Are all the results the same ?
parts:
Yes, inla.rmarginal only provides samples from marginal (posterior)
distributions, whereas inla.posterior.sample produces joint samples
from the entire model.
If the quantity you want to sample from only depends on a single
variable for which INLA has provided the marginal distribution, then
you could use inla.rmarginal (plus conditional data level sampling)
instead of inla.posterior.sample.

Finn
